title: White for harvest (John 4:31–38)
hook: lift up your eyes: the fields are already white

segments.voice: Yesterday, a woman at Jacob's well, and living water. Your line was never thirst. Did a glass of water remind you of who asked first? Day five hundred one.

While Jesus was talking at the well, the disciples were in town buying lunch. They come back with food and find him talking with a Samaritan woman. They're surprised, but nobody asks. The woman leaves her water jar right there and hurries back into town. Come, see a man who told me all things whatever I have done. Is he the Christ? Meanwhile the disciples unpack the food. Rabbi, eat. And he says something that makes them look at each other. I have food to eat that you don't know about. Did someone already bring him lunch?
screen: `THE DISCIPLES BRING LUNCH.` → `SHE LEAVES HER WATER JAR.` → `I HAVE FOOD YOU DON'T KNOW.`

segments.voice: This is John's pattern: Jesus says something deep, and someone takes it at ground level. Born again: back into the womb? Living water: where's your bucket? Food: who brought him a sandwich? Then he explains, in the Douay-Rheims: "My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, that I may perfect his work." Meat is the old word for food. What feeds him is doing his Father's will. And then he points. You have a saying, he tells them: four more months, and then the harvest. Farmers' wisdom. Planting's done, it's a long wait. "Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes, and see the countries, for they are white already to harvest." Countries here means the fields around them. White, because grain goes pale and gold when it's ripe. But picture what the disciples might actually see when they lift their eyes. Across the fields, coming out of the town, the Samaritans the woman has just told. A crowd walking toward them through the grain. Some readers have even wondered whether the white was the light clothing of that crowd. The text doesn't say. Either way, the harvest isn't four months off. It's walking up the road. Then: one sows and another reaps. You are reaping where others did the hard work. Readers name many sowers: the prophets, John the Baptist, Jesus himself. And here, in a small way, the woman with her jar. The disciples, who were busy with lunch and a little embarrassed at the scene, are being told they missed it. The harvest was ready, and the first worker in it was the last person they would have picked.
screen: `MY FOOD IS TO DO HIS WILL.` · `FOUR MONTHS AND THEN HARVEST?` · `LIFT UP YOUR EYES.` · `ONE SOWS, ANOTHER REAPS.` · then, large: `WHITE ALREADY TO HARVEST.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice who is ready to hear. Settle, and breathe. Lift your eyes, literally: look up from the screen, at the room, out the window. Then in your mind, look across the people in your week. Who has been asking questions lately? Who seems open, or lonely, or curious, or ready for a kind word? Maybe someone you'd never have picked. Don't plan a speech. Just notice them. If you pray, you can pray for them by name. If you don't, just keep their face in mind. The bell holds the time.
White for harvest. Fields pale and ripe, ready now, not in four months: Jesus's picture of the Samaritans coming to hear him. Today's word.
Your line: lift up your eyes. Today, look up from your phone three times, and notice one person each time. Day five hundred one.

howItsDone: Catholics hear this passage as part of the longer Gospel of the Samaritan woman on the Third Sunday of Lent in Year A, and the Church has often drawn on it in teaching about the mission to share the faith.

fork.setup: you're a disciple. you've brought back lunch, and Jesus says the harvest is ready now, not in four months. you lift your eyes. what do you see?
options: people from the town, coming toward you.
fork.reveal: the Samaritans, told by the woman, are coming out of the town. the harvest isn't four months away. it's walking up the road.

original.note: Greek: white, pale (John 4:35), the color of grain ripe for harvest.

trapdoor: what you thought: a farming proverb about patience.
what it means: the harvest is now, the Samaritans are already coming, and a woman the disciples overlooked helped sow it.
what a scholar hears: 'countries' in the Douay renders the Vulgate regiones (fields); the white crowd idea is a reading, not in the text.

sources.quoted: My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, that I may perfect his work.
Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes, and see the countries, for they are white already to harvest.

notes: Confirm exact Douay wording of John 4:35 ('see the countries, for they are white already to harvest').
The idea that 'white' may refer to the Samaritans' clothing is offered only as something some readers wonder; confirm or cut.
'Sower' identified with the woman is an interpretive move (many read the sowers as the prophets, John the Baptist or Jesus himself). Consider softening.
Third Sunday of Lent, Year A: John 4:5–42. Confirm.
Original: λευκαί (John 4:35, feminine plural agreeing with χῶραι). Confirm.
